prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing. A premium imaginative 3D product-campaign scene for Sorted, a UK money-planning app. Square 1:1 asset, no text or drawn interface. The concept is seeing what is coming before payday.
Scene is a small architectural calendar landscape in slate-blue darkness (#0f172a), physically lit, not neon. A sculpted ribbon of thick, individual calendar pages creates a sweeping S-shaped path from the lower left foreground around and behind one smartphone, receding to the upper right. The pages are ivory and dark slate with indigo binding tabs; they have only embossed little neutral squares, NO dates, words, tick marks or numbers. A few pages float free with crisp curling corners and visible paper thickness. At the end of the path a small upright satin indigo doorway/panel, NOT a lock or shield, implies the next pay period. Use tactile paper, brushed titanium, beautiful soft reflections, cinematic raking light, deep but legible shadows. No decorative sparkles, no coins, no rockets, no charts.
For compositing, a single large upright titanium smartphone must face directly towards the camera, perfectly front-on, parallel vertical sides, no rotation. Device occupies approximately x=34% to 70%, y=8% to 91%. Its dark blank screen is uniformly #0f172a, slim bezel, round corners and a small camera pill. No scenery overlaps the screen interior. The calendar path wraps around the outside and gives dramatic physical depth. Screen is reserved for our real app capture later. Smartphone and calendar are the only focal subjects.
Composition: asymmetrical, sweeping path concentrated bottom-left and right background, product lifted just above a matte slate platform, generous breathing room. Professional Cinema4D/Octane-like product rendering, attention-grabbing editorial advertising, not a dashboard illustration. Colour only slate, silver, white and solid indigo #4f46e5. No violet gradients, red, lettering, logos, currency signs, labels, UI or watermark.
note: No generated UI or figures. The campaign composites real production components in the browser.
